Hi Maya — thanks for taking the call. I paid for this consultation and have limited time, so I want to be efficient and end up with a dinner I can actually book tonight or soon.

Quick context about me:
- Staying around Beyoğlu (Taksim/Galata) — ideally something within ~30 minutes from there.
- Visiting Istanbul for a week and want an authentic, local dining experience (not touristy). I’m fascinated by meyhane/seafood, grilled meats (kebap), and Anatolian regional cooking. Open to adventurous dishes; no allergies.
- Budget: roughly USD 50–100 per person (including drinks).
- Prefer dinner around 8:00 PM on any evening this week (I can be flexible if one place is much better another night).

What I need from you in this call (please be specific and practical):
1. Two restaurant recommendations for dinner (I’ll choose one to book). For each restaurant include:
   - Why it’s authentic/why locals go there (not just social-media hype).
   - What type of place it is (meyhane, lokanta, meze bar, kebap house, chef-driven, seafood, etc.).
   - Signature dishes I should order (1–3 must-tries).
   - Price estimate per person (with drinks).
   - Typical crowd (locals/tourists/mix) and atmosphere (casual, lively, intimate).
   - How to get there from Beyoğlu (approx. time, best transport).
   - Whether they take reservations and the easiest way to reserve (phone/WhatsApp/website) — if you have the phone number or reservation link, include it.
   - Any booking tips (best table, what to request, anything to avoid).

2. A short recommendation of which of the two you think is the best fit for an authentic, memorable dinner for me (given my preferences and budget), and why.

3. If either place is likely fully booked, give one quick backup suggestion.

I’m ready — please give the two restaurant options with the details above, and then I’ll pick one to book.

Option 1: Çiya Sofrası (Kadıköy)  
- Why it’s authentic / why locals go: This is a long-running Kadıköy institution focused on Anatolian regional cooking—lots of “forgotten” village recipes and seasonal dishes that change daily. It’s famous with Istanbul food people and very locally driven (high local popularity), not built around views or social-media staging.  
- Type of place: Chef-driven Anatolian lokanta/meze-focused restaurant (regional Turkish).  
- Must-try dishes (ask what’s best that day):  
  1) Daily-changing Anatolian meze selection from the counter (pick a few)  
  2) İçli köfte (if available)  
  3) One of the lamb regional dishes + a regional dessert (they often have specialties you won’t see elsewhere)  
- Price estimate per person (with drinks): Roughly 700–1,000 TRY depending on how many meze/dishes you order and alcohol (food averages around 450 TRY; drinks push it up). Fits your USD 50–100 range.  
- Typical crowd / atmosphere: Mostly locals, plus food-focused visitors; bustling, casual, moderately noisy, very “real Istanbul” rather than polished.  
- How to get there from Beyoğlu (approx. time, best transport):  
  Best route: Taksim → F1 funicular to Kabataş (5 min) → ferry to Kadıköy (20–25 min) → walk ~10 min.  
  Total: typically ~35–50 minutes door-to-door depending on ferry timing.  
- Reservations / easiest way to reserve:  
  They’re generally walk-in friendly but can be busy. Phone: +90 216 330 3190. Website: https://www.ciya.com.tr (use mainly for info; booking is typically by phone/walk-in).  
- Booking tips:  
  - If you want an 8:00 PM dinner with less waiting, aim to arrive a bit early or be flexible by 20–30 minutes.  
  - Tell them you want “a tour of regional specialties” and ask what dishes are rare/hard-to-find—staff usually enjoys explaining origins.  
  - Because the menu changes daily, don’t go in with a fixed order; let the counter guide you.

Option 2: Sultan’s Delight Rooftop Restaurant (Sultanahmet)  
- Why it’s authentic / why locals go: The food is positioned as “Ottoman cuisine,” but in practice this place is primarily popular for the rooftop panorama and special-occasion dining. It’s very tourist-popular and less of a locals’ regular—more about the setting than a deep local, neighborhood feel.  
- Type of place: Rooftop Turkish/Ottoman dinner spot (scenic, special-occasion, semi-upscale).  
- Must-try dishes:  
  1) Ottoman lamb shank  
  2) Sultan’s Mixed Grill  
  3) Baklava platter + Turkish coffee/tea service  
- Price estimate per person (with drinks): Often ~1,600–2,200 TRY per person with drinks (base average meal cost is high). This can push the top of your USD 50–100 budget depending on what/how you order.  
- Typical crowd / atmosphere: Mostly tourists; elegant/romantic, moderate noise; great for views and photos rather than a “locals’ hangout.”  
- How to get there from Beyoğlu (approx. time, best transport):  
  Beyoğlu → to T1 tram line (via walking/short taxi to Karaköy or Kabataş) → tram to Sultanahmet area → short walk (it’s ~2 minutes from Hagia Sophia).  
  Total: about ~25–40 minutes depending on traffic and tram waits.  
- Reservations / easiest way to reserve:  
  Reservation page: https://www.sultansdelightistanbul.com/reserve  
  Phone: +90 212 512 8080  
- Booking tips:  
  - If you go, request an outdoor rooftop table near sunset (views are the main reason to choose it).  
  - Smart-casual works best.  
  - Be prepared for “touristy extras” (e.g., photo services); say no politely if you don’t want them.

Which is the best fit for you (authentic + memorable, given your interests and budget)  
Your preferences (meyhane/seafood vibe, grilled meats, adventurous Anatolian regional cooking, “not touristy”) align much more strongly with Çiya Sofrası. It’s the kind of place locals actually eat at, and it’s specifically built around regional variety and unusual dishes—more memorable in a culinary sense than a scenic rooftop.

Quick backup if one is slammed  
If Çiya is too busy at 8:00 PM, a reliable backup plan is: go to Kadıköy’s fish market area and choose a busy meyhane-style spot packed with locals (you’ll see the streets lively). Go earlier (7:00–7:30) to reduce wait, and do a meze + seafood-focused dinner.

I recommend Çiya Sofrası
